SILMO Paris Highlights Eyewear’s Future

The 2026 show brought more than 32,000 professionals to Paris for four days of eyewear, innovation, education, and awards.
by Zack TertelSeptember 29, 2026September 29, 2026

Share this:

  • Share on Threads (Opens in new window) Threads
  • Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email

0:00 / 1:56
Instaread

Last week, SILMO Paris 2026 welcomed more than 32,000 optical industry professionals to Paris Nord Villepinte for four days of new eyewear collections, technology, education, and industry awards.

International visitors accounted for 53% of attendance, with French professionals making up the remaining 47%. Attendees representing nearly 150 countries explored products and technology from more than 950 exhibitors and 1,500 brands across 80,000 square meters of exhibition space.

Technology and Eyewear Trends

SILMO Next’s Futurology and Tech Village explored developments in smart eyewear, artificial intelligence, predictive health, and other technologies through demonstrations, hands-on experiences, and educational sessions.

The show also held its first international hackathon focused on health applications for smart glasses. The winning project, Kimoo, was developed by Mourdjen Bari and Carla Nykiel on the HTC platform as an assistant designed to help people with ADHD stay focused, manage anxiety, and reduce procrastination.

In addition, more than 60 SILMO Talks addressed topics such as AI, smart glasses, health, retail, corporate social responsibility, and changes affecting optical professions.

Design Awards and Trends

The 33rd SILMO d’Or awards recognized products across 14 categories, including children’s eyewear, sport, vision, low vision, smart eyewear, technological innovation, and frame design. Chaired by Joachim Froment, a Brussels-based industrial designer and creative director and co-founder of the Futurewave studio, SILMO d’Or celebrated the dialogue between design, technology, and the wearer experience.

SILMO also recognized sustainability and emerging talent. Andy Wolf received the Committed Company Award, while Savannah College of Art and Design student Sophia Denison won the Optic Design Contest for DREAMSCAPE.

Jessica Gowing, principal optometrist at Great Ormond Street Children’s Hospital in London, received the International Optician of the Year Award.

In addition, The Trends Forum highlighted four directions expected to influence eyewear design:

  • Fancy. Unapologetic fantasy.
  • Charisma. Inspired contrast.
  • Adrenaline. Vibrant technology.
  • Aura. A return to 1990s glamour.

SILMO Paris will return Sept. 24-27, 2027, the show’s 60th anniversary.
